name: @adrata/starfield-mcp

tools.name: connect_workspace
tools.description: Connect your Adrata workspace via OAuth 2.0. Opens a browser window for authorization. By default the connection is READ-ONLY (least privilege): search/read companies, people, opportunities, pipeline, buyer groups, signals and analytics, plus the governed AI dispatcher for reads. Pass writeAccess:true to additionally request the CRM write scopes (companies, people, buyer groups, opportunities, actions, tasks) so create/update/delete work from this client; you will see them on the consent screen and can decline. Workspace administration and enrichment spend are never requested and always require a signed-in human session. The capability summary returned is derived from the scope the server actually granted, not from what was requested.

writeAccess.description: Request CRM write scopes in addition to read. Defaults to false (read-only).

tools.name: disconnect_workspace
tools.description: Disconnect your Adrata workspace. Revokes OAuth tokens and clears local credentials. Enterprise tools will no longer be available after disconnecting.

tools.name: workspace_status
tools.description: Check which credential this MCP server is actually running on, what tier it grants, which workspace it is acting in, and whether that credential still works. Run this first when a tool returns 401 or 403 — it names the credential in play and what to do about it.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces the authenticated user is actually a member of, with their role in each. Use before switch_workspace when a user belongs to more than one workspace.

tools.name: switch_workspace
tools.description: Switch the active workspace for the authenticated user. Subsequent tool calls read and write in the new workspace. Use list_workspaces first to get valid IDs.

tools.name: search_capabilities
tools.description: Search the authorized capability registry without loading schemas into context. A branded server fixes the namespace to its product. Search is discovery only: describe one exact result before run_capability, and never execute a fuzzy result.

query.description: Plain-language intent. Empty lists a bounded sample.

namespace.description: Optional only on the unprofiled server; a product profile cannot search another product.

tools.name: describe_capability
tools.description: Resolve one exact, versioned capability reference and return its input schema, risk, and execution metadata. This never executes the capability.

ref.description: Exact /product/domain/action reference; never a fuzzy search phrase.

tools.name: run_capability
tools.description: Run one exact capability through the governed dispatcher. Defaults to preview for every call. Set dryRun:false to execute reads, including paid provider reads and enrichment. Live writes remain subject to server-bound approval, reason, policy, and idempotency controls. Product profiles refuse references outside their namespace.

dryRun.description: Defaults true. Set false only after reviewing the exact schema and preview.

confirmationToken.description: Single-use server-bound token when required. Send dryRun:false to redeem; dryRun:true preserves the token.

confirmSpend.description: Deprecated no-op: paid reads no longer need a spend acknowledgment.

idempotencyKey.description: Required by governed live writes. Reuse the same key on retry.

tools.name: list_agent_tasks
tools.description: List long-running agent/background tasks with status and progress.

tools.name: create_agent_task
tools.description: Create a long-running agent/background task for research, enrichment, auditing, or custom workflow automation.

type.description: Task type such as account_research, lead_enrichment, sequence_optimization, pipeline_review, or custom

tools.name: get_agent_task
tools.description: Get detail, progress, and result for a long-running agent/background task.

tools.name: cancel_agent_task
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running agent/background task.

tools.name: list_webhook_events
tools.description: List supported outbound webhook event types, payload schemas, and examples.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: List outbound webhook subscriptions for the workspace.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Create an outbound webhook subscription. Returns the signing secret once; store it securely.

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description: Update an outbound webhook subscription URL, events, active flag, description, or filter expression.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete an outbound webhook subscription.

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description: Queue a signed webhook.test delivery to validate a subscription endpoint.

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.description: List recent delivery attempts for a webhook subscription.

tools.name: get_webhook_delivery
tools.description: Get status, response body, and retry metadata for a webhook delivery attempt.

tools.name: replay_webhook_delivery
tools.description: Replay a failed or previous webhook delivery.

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Get the currently authenticated user.

tools.name: who_am_i
tools.description: Get your user profile with usage statistics — tier, top tools used, recent activity, saved memories count, and industries researched. Useful for understanding your Adrata context.

tools.name: get_app_access
tools.description: Read own apps or administrator member/workspace grants. Read first before proposing a grant replacement.

tools.name: manage_app_access
tools.description: Administrator-only replacement of the COMPLETE workspace product set or one member app set. Omitted grants are revoked; workspace-wide grants remain effective after per-seat removal. Preserve unrelated grants. Previews by default; live writes require dryRun:false, approved:true, reason and idempotencyKey. Uses the same administrator check as Settings.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Returns a preview of the exact call instead of performing it. Set false to execute.

approved.description: Required (true) for a live write. Records that the caller confirmed the mutation; it does not by itself grant scope.

reason.description: Required for a live write. Recorded as the audit reason (X-Adrata-Reason).

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live write. Sent as Idempotency-Key so a retry cannot double-apply.

tools.name: get_workflows
tools.description: Read workflow library, packs, activity and approval stories, builder vocabulary, or an unsaved prompt draft. Pending approval is not execution.

tools.name: manage_workflow
tools.description: Create/edit/on/off workflows, change tell/ask/do, replay evidence, install/activate packs, or approve/edit/skip waiting runs. check_now evaluates and drains up to 25 queued runs across the entire workspace. Activation and approvals may execute configured actions. Live writes require explicit approval, reason and stable idempotencyKey.

tools.name: get_data_wallet
tools.description: Read the active workspace token wallet. The API requires a current owner or administrator membership. Amounts are exact decimal token strings; spendable already excludes held tokens. Commercial credits are separate. An uninitialized wallet is explicitly unavailable, never a fabricated zero balance. This tool cannot spend, refill, create or change a wallet.

tools.name: upgrade_account
tools.description: Open the Adrata Edition signup page in your browser to upgrade your account. Free users get a 14-day Pro trial (no credit card required). Pro users can manage their subscription. Enterprise users are directed to schedule a demo.

plan.description: Target plan: "pro" for self-serve upgrade, "enterprise" for sales contact. Defaults to "pro".

tools.name: check_subscription
tools.description: Check your current Adrata subscription plan, usage limits, trial status, and billing details. Works at all tiers: free users see upgrade options, pro users see usage and trial countdown, enterprise users see full workspace subscription details.

tools.name: get_workspace_settings
tools.description: View your workspace configuration, enabled modules, rate limits, user count, and subscription details. Use this to understand what features are available. Enterprise only.

tools.name: get_work_item_field_changes
tools.description: Read recorded edits to one card, newest first: field, previous and new values, actor, timestamp, reason and its source. Assignee names are current workspace directory labels; stored ids remain the historical values. Truncation is explicit. An empty result means no field changes were recorded, not that the card was never edited; older edits may predate recording. Reasons are the writer’s account, not independent QA evidence. Credential identifiers and worker capabilities are never returned.

tools.name: get_work_item_verification
tools.description: Read the current verification level (Full QA by default), exact definition snapshot, review expiry, owner capability and separate Confirmation acceptance. Read again before an approval; a stale snapshot cannot authorize a move.

tools.name: set_work_item_verification
tools.description: Choose Full QA or Confirmation with explicit owner approval of the current snapshot. This does not move the card or grant QA credit. Previews by default; only the server-authorized owner may make a live selection. Confirmation still needs criterion-local proof and deployed evidence before promotion.

tools.name: list_my_work_items
tools.description:
The cards that are YOURS, across every board in the workspace, ordered the way a developer actually picks: parked cards last (Deep backlog is where work was deliberately shelved, and offering it back argues with whoever parked it), then escalated first (the top band of each card's OWN scheme — a P1 is never equated with a Critical), then by the board's own left-to-right flow so the earliest active stage comes first, then longest-waiting. Production sits at the end of that flow, so nothing is picked up from it either.

"Yours" is TWO things: cards you OWN (you are the assignee, carrying it end to end) and cards whose CURRENT PASS you hold (you took it at a stage — the QA case). Both appear here, and each card carries assignee and handler so you can tell which of the two put it in front of you. A QA person owns none of the cards they are testing, so a queue keyed only on the assignee would tell them they had no work while four cards sat on their bench.

"You" is resolved from the authenticated token. There is deliberately NO parameter naming a user, and the endpoint refuses one rather than ignoring it — otherwise one agent could read another developer's queue through the very tool meant to keep them off each other's cards. To see somebody else's work, read their board with get_work_board.

Start here for "what should I work on". With includeUnassigned it also returns the cards nobody owns AND nobody is handling, which are the ones free to take (move_work_item with claim:true).

includeUnassigned.description: Also return the cards nobody owns and nobody is handling — the pool that is genuinely free. Use it when your own queue is empty, instead of pulling whole boards and eyeballing them. Note this is NOT "free QA passes": a card an engineer owns, waiting untaken in a QA column, is free to HANDLE but not free to own, so it stays off this list — read the QA columns with get_work_board for those.

boardId.description: Narrow to one board. Omit for every board.

limit.description: Cap each list. Defaults to 50; a queue that needs a second page is not a queue.

tools.name: list_work_boards
tools.description: List the work boards in the connected workspace. Returns each board id, name, the company it is run for (if any), and the tag scheme its cards are read under. Start here — every other board tool needs an id from this list.

tools.name: get_work_board
tools.description: Read one board whole: its columns (each with its own staleness policy) and every card on it. The card list carries columnId, enteredColumnAt, position, and the stored tag — everything needed to reason about what is stale and what matters.

tools.name: get_work_item
tools.description: Read one card by id: title, body, product, assignee, reporter, creator, its stored tag, and how long it has been in its current column. THREE DIFFERENT PEOPLE can appear on a card and they answer different questions: `assignee` is who is doing it (and changes hands over the card's life), `reporterPersonId` is the customer who asked (only on a card ingested from email), and `createdBy` is the teammate who wrote the card — resolved to a name, never changing, and the person to ask what the card meant. An absent `createdBy` means the card predates creator tracking, not that nobody made it.

tools.name: get_work_item_worker_lease
tools.description: Read who, if anyone, is actively running this card’s current QA pass. Returns the accountable teammate, declared agent/session labels, and Live or Stalled freshness. It never returns the bearer token, fencing value, or credential identity.

tools.name: get_work_item_worker_activity
tools.description: Read the human-readable worker lifecycle for one card: claim, conflict, renewal, stall, release, handoff, and audited takeover. Entries carry only public teammate/agent/session labels and timestamps; capability and credential material never appear.

tools.name: claim_work_item_qa_pass
tools.description: Take one named card’s current Staging QA1 or Staging QA2 pass without changing its durable owner. A winning response includes the current acceptance criteria and the recorded-QA rules you must follow. The bearer and fence stay process-private; later heartbeat and release tools use them without putting them in the conversation. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

runLabel.description: Concise public session label, not a transcript or secret.

workerLabel.description: Concise public worker label, not a transcript or secret.

tools.name: claim_next_work_item_qa_pass
tools.description: Atomically choose and take the first workable QA pass for ONE exact product in ONE requested gate across every board this worker can see. Product is read from the card, never inferred from the board that happens to hold it. QA1 and QA2 pools must name their gate explicitly; a QA1 drain can never consume QA2 work and vice versa. Concurrent sessions receive distinct cards; one MCP worker holds at most one pass at a time. An empty result is TWO different situations and the response tells them apart: an empty skippedBlocked means no eligible pass remains in that product/gate, so move to another lane; a non-empty skippedBlocked means there IS work here and every card is waiting on another card, so read the blockers rather than re-claiming. The response returns the selected board and card, explains the selection, and carries the exact acceptance criteria and recorded-QA requirements. Capability material stays inside this MCP process. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

qaGate.description: Exact gate this worker pool is allowed to drain.

product.description: Exact card product to drain, such as Adrata or Starfield, across all visible boards.

runLabel.description: Concise public session label, not a transcript or secret.

workerLabel.description: Concise public worker label, not a transcript or secret.

annotations.title: Claim Next Work Item Qa Pass

tools.name: heartbeat_work_item_qa_pass
tools.description: Keep the current MCP session’s claimed QA pass Live. The private bearer and fence are attached inside this process; they are never accepted as tool arguments or returned in the result. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

itemId.description: Card id returned by a winning claim in this MCP session.

tools.name: release_work_item_qa_pass
tools.description: Release or hand off the current MCP session’s QA pass. This closes the active lease but does not change the card’s durable owner. The private capability is supplied from process memory and removed after a successful release. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

itemId.description: Card id returned by a winning claim in this MCP session.

tools.name: record_work_item_qa_failure_and_release
tools.description:
Durably record why the current QA pass cannot proceed, then safely release the process-private lease without moving the card. Three dispositions, and only one of them flags:
- failed_criterion: the criterion is marked UNMET (un-ticked) and a comment records what failed, on which build, and what to check. NO FLAG: the unmet criterion is the finding, the card stays claimable, and a later pass that verifies the criterion again is the fix. This is one governed recovery recipe, not a new bug card and not a QA bounce.
- env_problem: your environment or seat was wrong (wrong host, stale build, no Mac runner, shared Chrome profile, expired session). A comment records it and the pass is handed off. NO FLAG and no criterion change: an environment problem is not a card defect. Check the build under test before choosing this.
- blocked_dependency: an explicit prerequisite no agent can satisfy. This one flags, as kind external_dependency (a credential, consent or vendor) or owner_decision (only the owner can answer; the owner is notified). Set blocksClaim:true only for those.
Every path releases the lease only after the finding is durably recorded; a claimable handoff is not a QA pass. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

itemId.description: Card currently claimed by this MCP worker.

blocksClaim.description: blocked_dependency only: stop pickup for a prerequisite no agent can satisfy. Refused for the other dispositions.

blockerKind.description: blocked_dependency only. Defaults to external_dependency; owner_decision notifies the workspace owner.

criterionId.description: Required for failed_criterion; the exact acceptance criterion contradicted.

buildSha.description: failed_criterion: the exact build the criterion failed on (7-40 hex). Recorded in the comment so a later pass can tell a fix from a retest of the same build.

details.description: Concrete observed failure or blocker and the recovery needed. For blocked_dependency the first sentence becomes the flag reason (280 characters max) and the rest is kept in the flag comment.

idempotencyKey.description: Required live base key; child writes derive stable endpoint-specific keys.

annotations.title: Record Work Item Qa Failure And Release

tools.name: requeue_work_item_qa_after_fix
tools.description: Clear a failed QA card’s waiting-for-fix flag only after a different exact build has been deployed and its relationship to the failed build has been checked. This does not claim or certify the card; it clears the resolved hold or failure handoff before a fresh independent QA pass. The clear reason durably records both SHAs and the fix/deployment reference. The worker must verify ancestry in source control before calling this tool; this endpoint rejects the unchanged SHA but does not pretend to be a Git ancestry oracle. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

itemId.description: Flagged QA card left in place by record_work_item_qa_failure_and_release.

repairedFlagGeneration.description: The flag.generation captured for the failure actually repaired. Never substitute a newer flag generation without resolving that failure.

failedBuildSha.description: Exact lowercase 40-character SHA of the build that failed.

deployedBuildSha.description: Exact lowercase 40-character SHA of the newer deployed descendant build.

details.description: How ancestry and deployment were verified, including the fix PR or deployment reference.

annotations.title: Requeue Work Item Qa After Fix

tools.name: get_work_item_history
tools.description: Read a card's column transitions, newest first: which column it came from, which it went to, when it entered and left, who moved it, and why. This is the audit trail the stage timer is derived from — use it to answer "how long did this actually take" rather than guessing from the current column.

tools.name: get_work_item_delivery_evidence
tools.description: Read the four facts that must never be collapsed into one status: the card's workflow column, linked pull-request state, exact-SHA staging presence, and exact-SHA production presence. Use this before calling a card shipped or treating the Production column as proof. Unknown means Adrata has no trustworthy evidence; it never means the work is absent. This tool is read-only and does not move the card.

tools.name: list_work_item_acceptance_criteria
tools.description: Read the ordered, executable definition of done for one card. Each criterion says where to check, any starting state, what action to perform, and the observable result. A zero-length list is a finding: nobody has stated how QA can decide the card is done. `criteriaQuality` names criteria that cannot fail as written — an unfalsifiable result, a location that is not a place to stand, an unfinished clause. Correct those before executing them; a criterion turned green by reading it generously is worth less than an open one.

tools.name: list_work_item_qa_evidence
tools.description: Read the durable image/video QA receipts attached to one card. Returns governed metadata and availability, never a presigned content URL or storage capability. Use the card UI to review playback; use attach_work_item_qa_evidence to add a fresh receipt.

tools.name: audit_work_hub
tools.description: Audit every visible Starfield board as an operating ledger. Returns named findings for active cards without owners, active passes without handlers, missing definitions of done, missing work types or context, stale stages, truncated reads, and boards that could not be read at all. It does not award a vanity score and it does not mutate anything. A clean result means every board it COULD read has the minimum workflow facts required to operate from it — read `boards` against `boardsExpected` before treating it as coverage. Deployment truth remains a separate exact-SHA fact available through get_work_item_delivery_evidence.

tools.name: get_work_board_rollup
tools.description: Read several boards as one prioritisation view. Pass "all" for the implicit roll-up of every board in the workspace (it has no membership rows, so a board created a minute ago is already in it), or a roll-up id for a curated one. Each slice keeps its own board, company, staleness policy, and tag scheme — cards are ranked WITHIN their own scheme and never translated across schemes, so a P1 is never silently equated with a Critical.

rollupId.description: Roll-up id, or "all" (the default) for every board in the workspace.

tools.name: list_work_board_rollups
tools.description: List the curated roll-ups in the workspace. The implicit "all boards" roll-up is NOT in this list because it has no row — read it with get_work_board_rollup using rollupId "all".

tools.name: get_work_item_comments
tools.description: Read what people have SAID about a card, newest first: each comment's author, body, and timestamp. READ THIS BEFORE STARTING WORK, alongside get_work_item_history. The history says which columns a card passed through; the comments say WHY — a card that came back from QA has the reviewer's reason here, and repeating a rejected approach is the most expensive mistake available on this board. A comment marked withdrawn is still returned with its text: its author took the claim back, but somebody may already have acted on it, so it is context and not noise. If the card carries a `flag`, the reason it was raised is in this thread too.

tools.name: attach_work_item_qa_evidence
tools.description: Attach one finalized local image or video to the card's CURRENT claimed QA dwell. This is the whole governed flow: the MCP process reads and hashes the local file, asks Adrata for a private upload capability, uploads the bytes directly, renews the worker lease, finalizes server-side verification, and returns only the durable receipt. File bytes, the local path, presigned URLs, upload headers, lease bearer, and fence never enter the conversation. Claim the pass first and keep recordings synthetic/redacted. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

itemId.description: Card id returned by this MCP session’s winning QA claim.

criterionId.description: Acceptance criterion this recording proves. Required by the API when the card has criteria.

filePath.description: Local path to the finalized PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, MP4, or WebM. The path and bytes stay process-private.

declaredBuildSha.description: Exact lowercase 40-character deployed Git SHA tested by this recording.

declaredReviewerAgent.description: Agent/runtime declaration shown on the receipt; never invent an unknown value.

declaredReviewerModel.description: Model declaration shown on the receipt; use an honest unrecorded label rather than guessing.

summary.description: Short synthetic-safe result summary. Never paste a transcript, token, customer data, or sensitive URL.

durationMs.description: Final media duration for video, measured from the finalized file; omit for images.

checkpoints.description: Ordered video checkpoints beginning at 0; omit for images.

redactionConfirmed.description: Confirms synthetic/approved data and no visible credentials, tokens, customer data, or sensitive query values.

reason.description: Required for a live attachment: what journey was recorded and why it belongs on this criterion.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live attachment. Reuse the SAME key on retry.

tools.name: verify_work_item_qa_evidence_playback
tools.description: Record the separate fact that you REOPENED an already-uploaded QA video in the card UI and personally observed it load, play, seek, and enter fullscreen. Upload completion proves stored bytes only; never call this tool from an upload response or without exercising all four controls. The receipt is bound to the current claimed QA dwell and server-authenticated credential. In QA2 you may verify the current QA2 recording or the recording from the immediately preceding QA1 dwell. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

itemId.description: Card id currently claimed by this MCP worker.

evidenceId.description: Video evidence receipt id actually reopened in the signed-in card UI.

contentLoaded.description: True only after the video rendered usable media.

playStarted.description: True only after playback visibly started.

seekCompleted.description: True only after seeking to another point completed.

fullscreenEntered.description: True only after the video entered native or in-page fullscreen.

reason.description: Required live audit reason naming the playback review.

idempotencyKey.description: Required live key. Reuse the SAME key only for the same playback review.

annotations.title: Verify Work Item Qa Evidence Playback

tools.name: set_work_board_archived
tools.description: Hide or restore a board in the workspace catalogue without deleting anything. Archived boards disappear from normal board lists and roll-ups, but their cards, history, releases, QA flows, memberships, and evidence remain intact. Use this for obsolete, duplicate, or no-longer-operated boards; never manufacture a release or delete cards merely to clean up the board chooser. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

archived.description: true hides the board; false restores it.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Set false for a live change.

approved.description: Required true for a live change.

reason.description: Required for a live change: why this board is being hidden or restored.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live change.

tools.name: set_work_board_column_wip_limit
tools.description: Set or clear one board column's visible WIP ceiling. Exceeding the ceiling never blocks a move: the board renders the measured count and limit in red so daily Aligning can answer for it. Only a workspace admin may change this operating policy. Production and Deep backlog cannot have limits because they are output and parking columns, not work centres. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

wipLimit.description: Positive ceiling, or null to clear it (unlimited).

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Set false to change it.

approved.description: Required true for a live change.

reason.description: Required for a live change: why this capacity is right.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live change. Reuse on retry.

annotations.title: Set Work Board Column Wip Limit

tools.name: preview_work_item_acceptance_reaffirmation
tools.description: Read the exact current criterion definitions and preserved independent QA evidence for a legacy human-accepted Ready to Ship card. Returns a content digest for a separate explicit owner decision. Original acceptance scope remains unknown; this never repairs missing QA.

tools.name: reaffirm_work_item_current_acceptance
tools.description: Record a separate owner approval of the exact CURRENT scope and existing QA evidence from preview_work_item_acceptance_reaffirmation. Only the authenticated delegated OAuth owner can do this. The original legacy acceptance receipt stays unchanged and its original scope stays unknown. This neither verifies criteria nor fills missing QA receipts. Use only on the owner's explicit instruction after reviewing the preview and limitation. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

tools.name: move_work_item
tools.description:
Move a card to another column on the same board — and, outside QA, use claim:true to pick it up in the same action. The server does this in ONE transaction: it closes the card's open dwell, appends the transition to the history, records you as the handler of the pass the card is now on, and updates the card. Dropping a card into the column it is already in is a REORDER and deliberately does not restamp the stage timer.

A card carries TWO people and they are not interchangeable. The OWNER (assignee) is whoever carries the card end to end — the engineer who builds it, and the person a QA bounce sends it back to. The HANDLER is whoever took the pass the card is on right now, which at a QA gate is the tester and nowhere else is usually the owner. claim:true always takes the pass; it takes ownership ONLY of a card nobody owns. So a QA pick-up on an engineer's card leaves the engineer owning it, which is what makes the two-gate flow work at all.

QA PASSES ARE THE EXCEPTION. An executable QA worker must hold the process-private lease and fencing capability before it can write in Staging QA1 or Staging QA2. Use claim_work_item_qa_pass (or claim_next_work_item_qa_pass) after the card is in QA; never use move_work_item(claim:true) to take a QA pass. This connector refuses that legacy shape locally instead of sending an unfenced write the API must reject. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

toColumnId.description: Target column id. Must be a column on the SAME board — get it from get_work_board.

position.description: Sort position within the target column. Omit to append to the end.

claim.description: Pick this card up as part of a NON-QA move: it records YOU as the handler of the pass the card lands on, and makes you the owner only if the card has no owner. "You" is resolved from the authenticated token — there is no way to claim on somebody else's behalf. Staging QA1 and Staging QA2 use claim_work_item_qa_pass instead because every executable QA write must carry a process-private lease and fence. Taking a non-QA pass somebody else is already HOLDING is refused (see force). Re-claiming a non-QA pass you already hold is a no-op, not an error.

force.description: Take over a pass SOMEBODY ELSE IS HOLDING. Requires claim:true and a reason saying why — the reason is the only record that person will have of losing the pass mid-stage. It does NOT take the card off its owner: reassigning a card is a deliberate edit to its assignee, never a side effect of a move — and there is no board tool here that does it, so reassignment is a human act on the board (or an explicit PATCH via adrata_api_request). Do not reach for this to work around a refusal; a pass somebody is running is theirs.

Expires within five minutes. Server requires the authenticated owner’s delegated OAuth credential and preserves species agent. This is delegated authority, not cryptographic proof of human presence. receivingBuildSha is the live API build; reviewedBuildSha is the separately reviewed component build and must match receipt.commitSha.

Stored on the transition row and rendered in the card's history, so it is what a human reads in three weeks asking why this took a week. Placeholder reasons ("moved", "update") are refused.

IT IS A HUMAN ACT: the API refuses it to a program (403) before it reads the flag, so an agent setting it gets a refusal rather than a waiver. It is also NOT how a card gets parked — moving a card to Backlog or Deep backlog is a different kind of move and needs no override at all.

Every field is a REFERENCE somebody can re-check without trusting you: a SHA verified against main, a run id re-fetched from the vendor. There is deliberately no field for a sentence — that is what `reason` is for. Letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon and hyphen only, 8 to 128 characters; anything carrying a space or a newline is refused by the server AND by the column. Do not put transcript text, message bodies, tool output, or anything you were told in confidence anywhere in this receipt.

Use move_work_item for a column on the same board. A transfer needs BOTH destination ids so a column from a different board cannot be attached accidentally. Governed write: previews by default. tools.name: block_work_item
tools.description:
Record that one card CANNOT START until another lands. Use this for a real dependency — the fix that has to ship first, the fixture the test needs, the decision the work waits on — not for a note or a "related to". A recorded dependency changes what the queue hands out: a blocked card stops being offered as workable to a lane, and is instead shown with the blocker named, so the next agent does not pay a full read-and-release to rediscover it.

Reading direction is "itemId is blocked by blockedByItemId".

The blocker resolves ON ITS OWN when it reaches Ready to Ship or Production — there is nothing to unset, and no "resolved" flag to keep in step. A blocker parked in Backlog or Deep backlog still blocks, and the queue says so in those words, because that case needs an owner decision rather than a retry.

Cross-BOARD links are allowed (a CRO card blocked by a Starfield defect is the case this exists for). A cycle is refused: if the blocker already depends on this card, directly or through others, the write returns 409 rather than creating a loop in which no card could ever be started.

This says "do not start this yet". It NEVER says "this is already proved" — a dependency does not satisfy an acceptance criterion, and QA evidence is never inherited across a link. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

blockedByItemId.description: The card it is waiting on.

reason.description: Why this dependency is real, in a sentence. Required — this is what the next agent reads instead of re-deriving it.

approved.description: Required true for a live change.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live change.

tools.name: unblock_work_item
tools.description:
Remove a dependency that should not have been recorded — a link added in error, or one that turned out not to be real.

This is NOT how a dependency ends in the normal course. A blocker resolves by REACHING Ready to Ship or Production, which the queue derives on its own; deleting the edge instead would say the dependency never existed and lose why the card waited. Use this only to correct the record.

Removing an edge that is not there succeeds: the caller asked for a state, and that state is what they get. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

source.description: Who decided. An agent classifying a card is "model" — claiming "human" would launder a guess as a person's judgement.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Set false for a live change.

approved.description: Required true for a live change.

reason.description: Required for a live change: why this tag.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live change.

tools.name: set_work_item_kind
tools.description:
Set what KIND of work a card is: bug, story, or chore. This is a FIELD on the card, not a tag — it is orthogonal to urgency, so a card can be a bug AND Critical, and setting the kind never touches the tag (or the assignee, product, or body).

Pass kind:null to clear it back to UNTYPED. Untyped is a real state and is NOT the same as "chore": a card nobody has categorised has no category, and recording chore would put a decision on the record that nobody made. If you do not know what a card is, leave it alone or clear it — do not guess. Governed write: previews by default. tools.name: create_work_item
tools.description:
Create a card on a board. Lands in the named column, or in Backlog on a standard board when none is given.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ARE FIRST-CLASS RECORDS, not prose buried in `body`. Use `acceptanceCriteria` for the executable definition of done: where to check, any starting state, what action to perform, and the observable result. Author the proof route at the same time: `verificationRoute` is REQUIRED on every criterion, because an omitted route silently became `product` and that is what a browser recording is then demanded for. Use `engineering`/`both` with a plain-language `engineeringReason` when no meaningful product-person retest exists. The card and every criterion are replay-safe under one idempotency-key family, so a retry after a partial failure cannot duplicate either. If you cannot write criteria, capture what you know in `body`; the preview will mark the card as not ready rather than inventing outcomes nobody agreed to.

ONE CARD IS ONE QA JUDGEMENT. If your criteria list needs QA to make more than one call ("follows the OS theme" AND "the toggle persists" AND "every surface is restyled"), that is several cards, not one — a bounce from a multi-outcome card names nothing actionable. Implementation steps ("create a React hook", "rename the CSS variables") are never cards; they are lines inside one.

YOU DO NOT NEED TO SAY WHO IS CREATING IT. The card records its creator from your authenticated token — there is no parameter for it, and a body naming one is REFUSED rather than ignored, on the same rule as list_my_work_items. Creating is also not claiming: a new card arrives unassigned unless you name an owner, and you pick work up by moving it into an active column with move_work_item(claim:true), which is the act that also starts the stage timer honestly. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

title.description: What the card is. Keep it a statement of the work, not a label.

body.description: The request, evidence, and repro/context. Markdown. The executable definition of done belongs in acceptanceCriteria, not in this prose.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Executable definition of done. One independently checkable outcome per entry. Omit only for a thin capture that is not ready to build.

whereText.description: Surface, environment, account, or role to check. A place the next reviewer can stand, not the whole product — "the app" tells them nothing.

givenText.description: Starting state, when one is required.

thenText.description: Observable result that must follow. Name a checkable value, count, state, or exact message. A criterion that cannot fail cannot establish completion.

verificationRoute.description: REQUIRED. How this criterion gets proved. `product` needs a signed-in browser recording; `engineering` needs executed code/test/runtime proof; `both` needs BOTH and is the STRICTEST of the three, not a compromise. Choose from what the thenText says: can a browser DISPLAY the result? Then product. Is the result an ECS task definition, a migration receipt, a CI leg, an HTTP status contract, a log record, a vendor invoice or a test suite? Then engineering.

engineeringReason.description: Required for engineering or both: why no meaningful product-person retest exists.

product.description: Product tag — orthogonal to the board.

kind.description: What kind of work this is. OMIT IT unless the card plainly says: an absent kind means untyped, which is honest, where a guess is indistinguishable from a person's judgement once it is on the record. Change it later with set_work_item_kind.

columnId.description: Target column. Defaults to Backlog on a standard board.

OMIT IT unless somebody has actually agreed to own this — creating a card is not claiming it, and an unowned card in the backlog is the normal state of a backlog. Do not put yourself here to mark "I filed this": the card already records its creator.

This is grooming, not a comment: write where the check runs, the action, the observable result, and its proof route. verificationRoute is REQUIRED -- an omitted route silently became product, which then demands a browser recording for a criterion about a CI job. engineering and both require a plain-language engineeringReason. The server stores the criterion and its initial route audit receipt atomically. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

Choose from what the thenText says: can a browser DISPLAY the result? Then product. Is the result an ECS task definition, a migration receipt, a CI leg, an HTTP status contract, a log record, a vendor invoice or a test suite? Then engineering.

tools.name: classify_work_item_acceptance_criterion
tools.description:
Change WHICH KIND OF PROOF one existing acceptance criterion needs, and record who decided. Use this when a criterion is routed `product` but a signed-in browser could not establish it AT ALL — its `thenText` is about a test suite, a named source file, a migration receipt, an ECS task definition, a CI leg, an HTTP status contract, a log record or a vendor invoice. A criterion routed `product` by mistake is not merely mislabelled: it demands a recording of something that has no screen, so it can never legitimately pass, and the QA lane that draws it spends a whole pass discovering that.

THIS IS NOT A WAIVER, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT. `engineering` asks a reviewer for MORE than `product`, not less — an exact deployed build SHA, named executed code/test/configuration/runtime references, and a reviewer independent of the author (see record_work_item_criterion_engineering_proof). `both` requires BOTH and is the STRICTEST of the three. What `engineering` drops is the one demand that was never satisfiable: a browser replay of a thing that has no rendered surface. Both QA gates still run either way, and no route changes whether a criterion has been proved — only what would count as proving it.

SO ROUTE FROM THE CRITERION'S OWN WORDS, NOT FROM WHAT IS CHEAP TODAY. Can a browser DISPLAY the result its `thenText` asks for? Then it is `product` and it stays `product`. A fixture you do not have, an environment that is down, or a journey that is tedious to record are reasons to report a blocker, never reasons to reclassify. If the criterion carries a code fact AND a seller-visible outcome it is `both`, or leave it `product`; quietly splitting that difference downward is the one thing this tool could be used to launder.

`engineeringReason` is REQUIRED for `engineering` and `both` and REFUSED for `product`: say in plain language why no meaningful product-person retest exists, because a later reader has to trust the routing rather than re-derive it. `note` is the separate audit sentence for THIS act — why the classification is changing now.

The server refuses the change when the card is standing at a QA gate AND you are the credential that wrote the criterion, in the direction that adds the engineering claim or drops the product one. That is deliberate: reclassifying your own check out of the recording a reviewer just asked for is the exact move the rule exists to stop. Ask the reviewer to reclassify it, or say why on the card. Classification belongs at grooming. Every change writes a durable receipt carrying the previous route, the new one, both sentences, your credential, and the column and dwell the card was standing in. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

criterionId.description: Criterion id from list_work_item_acceptance_criteria — the `id`, not the `ordinal`.

verificationRoute.description: REQUIRED. The route this criterion should have had. `product` needs a signed-in browser recording; `engineering` needs executed code/test/runtime proof against an exact build; `both` needs BOTH and is the STRICTEST of the three, not a compromise.

engineeringReason.description: Required for engineering or both, refused for product: why no meaningful product-person retest exists. Plain language, 600 characters or fewer.

note.description: Why the classification is changing NOW — the audit note for this one act, distinct from engineeringReason, which is the standing claim about the criterion.

tools.name: edit_work_item_acceptance_criterion
tools.description:
Rewrite the WORDS of one existing acceptance criterion — its `whereText`, `whenText`, `thenText` or `givenText`. Use it when a criterion says the wrong thing: its `whereText` names a surface this card does not own, its `thenText` asks for something no observation could measure, or it cites a count, fixture or file name that has since changed and would now fail a reviewer who is looking at the right thing.

REWRITING ANY OF THE FOUR TEXTS CLEARS THE CRITERION'S SATISFACTION. The ticker, the column, the note, the dwell and the evidence link are all set back to NULL, and the card drops below its gate. That is deliberate and it is not a bug to work around: a tick is evidence about a SENTENCE, and the moment the sentence changes the evidence no longer refers to anything. Reordering alone does not clear it — only a change to the words does. So edit at grooming, before a pass has spent anything; editing a verified criterion costs a real recorded journey.

WHAT THIS TOOL MUST NOT BE USED FOR, and it is the only way it can do damage: narrowing a criterion because the product is failing it. If the product does not do what the criterion says, the fix is the product, or a bounce naming the criterion — never a sentence rewritten until today's behaviour passes. Afterwards a laundered criterion is indistinguishable from one that always said that, except in the receipt, so the receipt is the only thing standing between this tool and a definition of done that quietly tracks whatever was built.

PREFER THIS TO DELETION WHENEVER THE INTENT IS REAL. Most criteria that look impossible are merely mis-scoped — they ask this card to establish something the whole board owns. Rewriting keeps the intent on the record where a reader can still see what was wanted; deleting throws it away. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

whereText.description: New WHERE: the surface or system a reviewer looks at. Omit to leave unchanged.

whenText.description: New WHEN: the action the reviewer takes. Omit to leave unchanged.

thenText.description: New THEN: the observable result. Must be something a reviewer could see and disagree about. Omit to leave unchanged.

givenText.description: New GIVEN: the precondition. Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: delete_work_item_acceptance_criterion
tools.description:
PERMANENTLY REMOVE one acceptance criterion from a card, taking its history with it. Reach for this ONLY when a criterion is unsatisfiable BY CONSTRUCTION — when no evidence any reviewer could gather would ever discharge it. That is not a high bar being enforced; it is a card that can never leave its gate, and it costs a full pass every time a lane draws it and discovers why.

TWO SHAPES QUALIFY, and both were measured on this board:

GATE-AS-CRITERION. Its subject is the exit condition of the whole gate or the whole board rather than this card's own deliverable — "every criterion on every QA card carries a fresh receipt", "every card in QA2 is verified". A card cannot verify the queue it is standing in, and a criterion requiring a later gate to have run cannot be discharged from the earlier one.

PRODUCTION-CERTIFICATION. Its `whereText` is the production build after protected merge and deploy. Agents never move a card to Production and never certify production — that is the human owner's act by design — so no QA pass can discharge it at any level of effort. The observation is real and belongs in an acceptance note for the owner, not in a row that gates a QA lane.

WHAT DOES NOT QUALIFY, which is most of what will tempt you: a criterion that is merely hard, currently failing, blocked on a fixture you do not have, or blocked on an environment that is down. Every one of those is a BOUNCE or a BLOCKER — cheap, reversible, and visible to whoever can clear it. Deletion is none of those things. "I could not satisfy it" and "it cannot be satisfied" are different claims, and only the second one is this tool.

TRY `edit_work_item_acceptance_criterion` FIRST. In practice most impossible-looking criteria have real intent and an impossible SCOPE: rewriting one to the part this card actually owns keeps the intent legible to the next reader, where deleting erases the fact that the definition of done was ever larger. Delete when the intent itself does not belong on this card — not when its wording is wrong.

Say in `reason` which of the two shapes it is and what a reviewer would have had to produce, because after this call nothing downstream can reconstruct what was removed. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

reason.description: Required for a live write: which shape of unsatisfiable-by-construction this is (gate-as-criterion or production-certification) and what a reviewer would have had to produce. This is the only surviving record of what was removed.

tools.name: satisfy_work_item_acceptance_criterion
tools.description:
Tick one acceptance criterion with the evidence you actually observed.

WHERE AND WHEN YOU TICK FROM DECIDES WHAT THE TICK IS WORTH, and it is not a permission you can ask for. The grade is derived on every read from the card's CURRENT QA PASS and your server-derived credential:

  • `verified` — ticked during the card's CURRENT visit to Staging QA1 or Staging QA2 by an authenticated human, or by an agent credential distinct from the criterion author. In Staging QA2, that agent must also differ from the agent whose clean receipt opened Staging QA1.
  • `claimed` — everything else: a build-column tick, an earlier-pass tick, an agent checking its own criterion, the same AI trying to certify both gates, or legacy evidence with no provable credential identity.

EACH QA GATE IS ITS OWN GATE. A receipt belongs to the exact visit it was made in, not to the column's name. So a criterion verified in Staging QA1 reads `claimed` once the card reaches Staging QA2, and a card bounced out of QA1 and sent back needs checking again. This is not the board losing your evidence — the earlier pass stays in the card's activity and transition history. It is the board refusing to let one test present itself as two.

The human path is deliberately accountable rather than artificially independent: a sole human reviewer may verify a card they own or a criterion they wrote. The two-AI path remains independent by credential, and one AI cannot impersonate two passes. Nothing fails when a tick grades as `claimed`; inspect the returned grade and leave the card where the actual evidence supports it.

TICK WHAT YOU RAN, not what you believe. The card face prints met over total; the QA exit gate reads the VERIFIED count. So a card whose boxes were all ticked by its own author reads 5/5 on the face and still stops the gate — which is the design working. Ticking without running the check converts an honest "we shipped with two open" into a false "all met", and the false version is the one that gets believed later.

THE LATEST TICK IS THE ONE THAT COUNTS, and it REPLACES the one before it. The server writes the ticker, the credential, the column, the pass and the note in one statement, so a second tick overwrites the first — including its note. That is what makes two gates two gates: the QA2 reviewer re-ticks the same box to record their own pass, and a tick that could not be replaced would leave QA2 permanently reading QA1's receipt.

The cost is real and it is the note: re-ticking discards the previous ticker's evidence, and the criterion row only ever shows its current pass. If that evidence is worth keeping, put it on the card with comment_on_work_item BEFORE you re-tick. Do not re-tick a box merely to attach your name to somebody else's finished check. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

criterionId.description: Criterion id from list_work_item_acceptance_criteria — the `id`, not the `ordinal`.

note.description: OPTIONAL, and the most useful field here: the evidence. A build number, a PR or run link, or the caveat that makes the tick honest ("only checked on Safari"). Stored on the criterion and shown beside it, so it is what a release review reads instead of taking the tick on trust. Omit it when there is genuinely nothing to add — an invented note is worse than none.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Set false to record the tick.

approved.description: Required true for a live tick.

reason.description: Required for a live tick: the audit reason — how you checked this, not what the criterion already says. The evidence a human reads on the card is `note`.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live tick. Reuse the SAME key on retry.

tools.name: unsatisfy_work_item_acceptance_criterion
tools.description:
Un-tick one acceptance criterion, back to `unmet`. Use it when the check turns out not to hold, when it was ticked against the wrong build, or when it was ticked from a build column and has to be re-run at the gate to count as verified.

This exists so that ticking is safe to do. A box nobody can clear is a box people hesitate to tick, and that hesitation is exactly how a board ends up with a full checklist that nobody has ever touched — so shipping the tick without its counterpart would have left the same problem in a new shape.

It clears the WHOLE circumstance together — the ticker, the column, the note and the timestamp — never just the timestamp. Otherwise the next tick would inherit somebody else's evidence: a criterion re-ticked in Aligning would keep reading as verified in QA1, attributed to a person who was not there. So the cost is real, and it is the note: the first ticker's evidence is gone. If it is worth keeping, put it on the card with comment_on_work_item BEFORE you clear it.

Anyone who can see the card may un-tick, including somebody undoing another person's tick. The audit reason is the only record of why, so write it for them. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

tools.description:
Record that ONE acceptance criterion was checked LOCALLY, at a named commit, with the command that was run and where its output lives.

This is the gate in front of staging, and it is a different record from a QA receipt. A QA receipt says an independent credential re-ran a criterion against a deployment; this says the builder ran it on their own machine before asking for a deploy at all. It cannot be filed as QA evidence and it opens no QA gate.

A card is "Verified locally" — and only then reads "Ready for staging" on the board — when EVERY open criterion either has a passing local proof here or is tagged staging-only with a reason (tag_work_item_criterion_staging_only). tools.name: comment_on_work_item
tools.description:
Say something on a card: a question, a finding, or the reason a QA pass sent it back. This is the ONLY place to put a fact that contradicts the card — the ship-the-card skill tells you to say so on the card rather than silently fixing something else, and this is where that goes. Do NOT overwrite the card's body to make the point: the body is the original request, and rewriting it destroys the evidence of what was actually asked for.

A comment is deliberately small: no threading, no reactions, no formatting. One author, one paragraph, in order.

TO @-MENTION SOMEBODY, write the token `<@userId>` in the body — the id comes from the card's assignee, its history, or list_my_work_items. Anything else you type is literal text: writing "@noah" mentions nobody, which is deliberate. A mention means "see this" and NOTHING more — it does not assign the card, add a watcher, or raise a flag. Only workspace members resolve; a token naming anyone else stays as text and notifies no one. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

body.description: What you want to say. Plain text; newlines are kept. Capped at 2000 characters — longer than that belongs in the card description or a linked document. Use `<@userId>` to @-mention a workspace member; bare "@name" is literal text and mentions nobody.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Set false to post it.

approved.description: Required true for a live post.

reason.description: Required for a live post: why you are commenting. This is the audit reason, NOT the comment — the comment is `body`.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live post. Reuse the SAME key on retry: a replayed comment is just the same paragraph twice, which reads as you being emphatic rather than as a retry.

tools.name: flag_work_item
tools.description:
Flag unresolved work for the next repair and retest, or clear a flag once its reason is resolved. Ordinary failures remain visible and claimable.

A FLAG IS NOT A TAG. The tag says how urgent the work is; a flag records an unresolved problem. If a card is merely important, use set_work_item_tag.

THE REASON IS REQUIRED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and it is not the audit reason — it is the text read on the card. Raising says what failed, what you tried, and what remains to check; clearing says what resolved it. Agents may clear a resolved flag without a human handoff. Both directions append a comment, preserving the original failure and its resolution.

A FLAG HANDS THE CARD ON; IT DOES NOT HIDE IT. A failed test or an unsuccessful first repair is not an external hold. Leave it claimable so the next agent can investigate, repair, and independently retest. Clearing a flag does not certify acceptance criteria or replace either QA gate.

EVERY FLAG HAS A KIND. criterion_failure (a named criterion failed on a named build; prefer marking the criterion unmet with record_work_item_qa_failure_and_release), env_tooling (never blocks, expires after 24h — but do not flag environment or seat problems at all; record them as a comment), owner_decision (only the owner can answer; the owner is notified), external_dependency (a credential, consent or vendor). Omitted, the server infers external_dependency when blocksClaim is true and criterion_failure otherwise.

A REASON IS ONE SENTENCE PLUS THE UNBLOCK STEP, 280 characters at most. Put everything else in detail, which is kept in the flag's comment.

FLAGS CLEAR THEMSELVES when the card enters Ready to Ship, Production or Deep backlog, when the failed criterion is verified again, and when a deploy carries a criterion failure's fix. Do not downgrade a resolved flag: clear it and comment. A decision the owner delegated to you is a "Decided:" comment, not a flag.

PASS blocksClaim:true ONLY with kind owner_decision or external_dependency — the server refuses it for the other kinds. The hold remains until that prerequisite is satisfied and the flag is cleared with a resolution reason. Do not turn an ordinary test failure into an owner decision. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

flagged.description: true raises the flag; false clears it. Raising with the current flag.generation as expectedFlagGeneration is an EDIT: the reason changes and the generation, raise time and raiser stay, so a repairer holding that generation can still clear it. Raising without one is a new flag and renews the generation. Only an unflagged card becoming flagged increments the lifetime count (drawn on the board as a stack of pennants).

reason.description: REQUIRED. Raising: what is wrong with the card. Clearing: what resolved it. Shown on the card and appended to its comment thread — write it for the person who will read it, not for a log.

expectedFlagGeneration.description: Required when clearing: flag.generation captured for the failure actually resolved. When raising, pass the current generation to EDIT that flag instead of raising a new one. A stale generation is refused with "The flag changed": reload the card and act on the current flag.

detail.description: Everything that does not fit the one-sentence reason. Kept in the flag comment, not on the card face.

blocksClaim.description: Whether this flag prevents claims. OMITTED MEANS FALSE: ordinary failed work remains claimable for repair and independent retest. Only kind owner_decision or external_dependency may pass true. Ignored when clearing.

tools.name: archive_work_item
tools.description:
Retire a card: done with, wrong, obsolete, or superseded. It leaves every active count — the board's own size, the roll-up, the personal queue, velocity, capacity, the roadmap's card counts, the criterion standings — and stops being offered to a QA lane.

This is the COMMON case and it is recoverable. Reach for it whenever a card should stop being counted; if you find yourself wanting to hide a card by moving it somewhere nobody looks, this is the tool you actually wanted.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Do not use move_work_item to Backlog or Deep backlog to retire a card. Those are PARKING: work still intended, later — it stays in every count, which is correct for parked work and wrong for work nobody will ever do. Retiring is the other thing, and it is the only one that takes the card out of the numbers.

NOTHING IS DESTROYED. The card keeps its board, its column, its column history, its acceptance criteria and its QA evidence. It stays readable by get_work_item and it comes back with unarchive_work_item. The exclusion is a read filter, never a row removal — QA receipts bind to those column dwells and deleting them would leave every receipt on the card unexplainable. Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — a duplicate move would read as the card having bounced between columns).

reason.description: REQUIRED. Why this work will not be done. Shown on the card and appended to its comment thread — write it for the person who finds the card in six months and wonders what happened to it. "obsolete" is not an answer; "superseded by <card>, the API changed under it" is.

approved.description: Required true for a live change.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live change. Reuse the SAME key on retry — retiring also appends a comment.

tools.name: delete_work_item
tools.description:
Retire a card as DELETED rather than archived. Rare, and deliberate.

PREFER archive_work_item. The two do the same thing to the numbers; the difference is what the record says about the decision, and "archived" is the honest word for almost every card. Use this only when the card should never have existed — a duplicate, a mis-filed capture, something created by an integration by mistake.

IT IS STILL A SOFT DELETE. The row survives and unarchive_work_item brings it back. That is not a loophole: this board is the audit record behind a two-gate QA process, and a hard delete would cascade away the column history that every QA receipt binds to.

YOU MUST ECHO THE CARD'S EXACT TITLE in confirmTitle. Read the card first with get_work_item; do not guess it from the id or from a list you are half sure of. The echo is the whole safeguard — it is what makes this something you cannot do by accident inside a loop.

tools.name: list_work_scopes
tools.description:
The containers ABOVE the cards: every initiative, epic, and feature in the workspace, flat, each with its parent id and its counted progress (cards / shipped / in QA). This is the roadmap of record — Starfield owns every epic. An epic whose source_roadmap_slug is set was imported once from the repository's former spoq/epics/ tree; that slug is provenance only, and the scope is edited in Starfield like any other.

Progress is COUNTS, never a percentage: "7 of 12 shipped" is honest where "58%" is a feeling. A scope with zero cards is a real state (a commitment nobody has broken down yet), not an error.

Use this before add_to_roadmap: if an epic with the same intent already exists, the roadmap needs your card or feature under it, not a duplicate epic beside it.

tools.name: add_to_roadmap
tools.description:
Add an idea to the roadmap as a PROPOSED epic — the "add this to the roadmap" verb. Creates an epic-level scope (status: proposed, i.e. below the line) through the same endpoint the app uses, so it appears on the Roadmap page immediately.

The scope IS the epic. Starfield is the roadmap of record (company/decisions/2026-09-25-starfield-is-the-backlog.md): there is no EPIC.md to write and no pull request to open. Break the epic down with create_work_item; evidence such as audits and designs goes in documents/ in the repo, cited from the scope.

DO NOT use this for work that belongs under an existing epic — check list_work_scopes first and file a card (create_work_item) or ask a human to add a feature instead. A roadmap of near-duplicate epics is how a roadmap stops being read.

Governed write: previews by default. A live write requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey (reuse the SAME key on retry — the server replays instead of creating a second epic).

title.description: What the epic is, as a statement of the outcome. This exact string becomes the epic's title on the Starfield roadmap.

tools.name: move_work_scope_under
tools.description:
Re-file a roadmap container under a different parent — "move this epic under that initiative". An epic created before its initiative existed, or filed under the wrong product, can be moved without recreating it, so its features and cards come with it and the initiative's counted progress picks them up.

The ladder is strict and the server refuses anything else, naming the level that WOULD have been allowed: an epic moves only under an initiative, a feature only under an epic, an initiative has no parent. A scope cannot move under itself or its own descendant. parentScopeId null lets the scope stand alone (legal at every level). Get ids from list_work_scopes.

Re-sending the same target is a no-op, so a retry cannot move anything twice.

Governed write: previews by default. A live move requires dryRun:false plus approved:true, a reason, and an idempotencyKey.

scopeId.description: The epic or feature being moved, from list_work_scopes.

parentScopeId.description: The new parent: an initiative for an epic, an epic for a feature. Pass null to let the scope stand alone.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true. Set false to move it.

approved.description: Required true for a live move.

reason.description: Required for a live move: why this container belongs under that parent.

idempotencyKey.description: Required for a live move.
